scope: NACA0012 airfoil drag at Re=1000, alpha=0, 2D D2Q9 MRT, surface-only vs all-solid Ladd MEM

reference.source: Kurtulus 2015 (IJMAV 7(3):301) prose Cd(0deg)~0.12; independently cross-checked by Di Ilio et al. 2020 (arXiv:2006.10487) Table 1: Cd=0.119 (HLBM) / 0.119 (XFOIL) -> 0.8% agreement. The old script value 0.105 has no source and was rejected (-12.5%).

caliber_conflict:
The two standard MEM calibers disagree in OPPOSITE directions on this friction-dominated airfoil, and the apparent 'all-solid passes' result is a CANCELLATION ARTIFACT, not accuracy:
  * surface-only MEM: +118.7% (C64) / +110.7% (C128) -> grossly OVER-predicts, and does not converge (-8% over the ladder).
  * interior pseudo-force is NEGATIVE (-0.1068 / -0.1001) -- the opposite sign to the cylinder/sphere case.
  * all-solid = surface + interior, so a +118% surface error is partly cancelled by a -89% interior error
    to land at +17%/+15% vs 0.105 (or +2.3%/+0.9% vs 0.12).  Two errors cancelling is NOT a verified caliber.
  * Cross-check: Cd_all span is 1.4% (looks converged) but Cd_surface span is 8% (diverges) -- the two
    calibers disagree on whether this case converges at all.
diagnosis:
At alpha=0 the drag is friction-dominated (Cl = 0 to 4e-6, symmetric).  With a chord of only 64-128 cells the
boundary layer spans 2-4 cells, so neither the surface-restricted momentum-exchange sum nor the interior term
is a defensible force at this resolution.  The earlier performance blocker (collide_mrt 130 ms/step + stream 97
ms/step) was fixed by benchmarks/pending/naca_0012/fast_kernel.py (elementwise MRT + torch.roll streaming,
288 -> 36 ms/step, 6-8x), which is what made these two 60000-step ladders possible at all.
verdict:
NOT ACCEPTED.  surface-only MEM is +110% and non-convergent; all-solid appears to pass only because its
negative interior term cancels the surface error.  Recorded honestly rather than promoted on a cancellation artifact.
